name: parr-flash-council-office
prompt: A tall portrait colour photograph taken straight on at midday inside the reception of a tired modern British council office: a beige laminate counter with a scuffed edge, a red plastic take-a-number dispenser on a pole, a rack of sun-faded leaflets, a row of moulded blue plastic chairs bolted together, grey carpet tiles and a wall clock. Five people stand in a neat queue in front of the counter, side-on to us, heads tipped back, staring up at an enormous stack of loose white paper that fills the whole space behind the counter and climbs straight up through a hole where a ceiling tile has been knocked out, the dangling tile hanging from its grid. Taped to the front of the stack at eye level is one laminated A4 sheet printed in plain black capitals: "THE RULES". Each of the five wears a knitted balaclava in a different loud colour, lime green, bubblegum pink, traffic-cone orange, cobalt blue and lemon yellow, with no eye, nose or mouth openings; a thick white ring is stitched around the whole front of each head, and a small red triangle with rounded corners sits high inside the ring over the wearer's left eye, toward two o'clock as seen from the camera, never centred. They wear today's cheap clothes: shiny polyester tracksuits, a market-stall anorak, a puffer jacket, collars zipped up over the necks of the balaclavas, cuffs pulled over the wrists, plain knitted gloves on every hand, not a patch of skin anywhere. One holds a paper ticket. Shot from chest height at a middle distance with a wide-angle lens, slightly lower than eye level, the frame packed edge to edge with clutter. Lit only by a harsh flash fired from on the camera, so faces of fabric pop in hard, oversaturated colour, each figure throws a crisp dark shadow onto the beige wall behind, the laminate counter flares with a hot white glare and the background falls a touch darker. Candid documentary snapshot on slow colour negative film, punchy and slightly garish, cheap and deadpan, no one posing.
